title: Original ball found but is unplayable
question: You find your original ball within 3 minutes, but it's stuck up against a tree and you can't play it. Are you allowed to keep playing your provisional ball instead?

choices.text: Yes, you can play the provisional ball instead of the original
No, you must continue with the original ball and use the unplayable ball rule
Yes, but only with a penalty stroke
You can declare both balls lost and replay your shot

explanation: You must continue with your original ball, even if it’s unplayable. If you can't play it, you have to use the options under the unplayable ball rule.

juniorVersion.title: You Find Your Ball But It's Stuck
juniorVersion.question: You find your ball next to a tree. You can't hit it because it's blocked. Can you use your other (provisional) ball instead?

choices.text: Yes, you can play your provisional ball instead
No, you have to use your first ball and use the unplayable rule
Yes, but only if you add a penalty shot
You can say both balls are lost and play again from where you hit

juniorVersion.explanation: You must keep playing your first ball, even if it’s stuck and you can’t hit it. You need to use the unplayable rule to move it.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: A second ball you play in case you can’t find your first ball.
A rule that lets you move your ball if you can’t hit it, by taking a penalty.

juniorVersion.teachingTip: Act out being stuck by a tree and show how to use the unplayable ball rule.
likelyMisconceptions: Kids may think they can always use their provisional ball if their first one is in a bad spot.
They might not know what 'unplayable rule' means.
